'''Suresh Raj Sharma''' ({{langx|ne|डा. सुरेशराज शर्मा}}; 22 July 1940 – 23 September 2026) was a Nepali educationist who was the founder [[Chancellor (education)|Vice Chancellor]] of [[Kathmandu University]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XXBmAAAAMAAJ|title=Nepal Who's who|date=1997|publisher=Research Centre for Communication and Development|pages=600|language=en}}</ref> 

Sharma held a Ph.D. in Chemistry from [[London South Bank University]], London. He was the first executive director of the Council for Technical Education and Vocational Training, Member Secretary in National Education Committee, Member of National Commission for UNESCO, and National Delegate to the [[SAARC]] Technical committee on science and technology. Sharma was a well-known educational administrator. He made significant contribution to the development of education policy in Nepal. He had a number of books, research papers, articles, secondary school curriculum textbook and many more to his credit.

He was a lifelong member of the board of trustees of Kathmandu University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kathmandu University {{!}} Board of Trustees |url=https://ku.edu.np/board-of-trustees |access-date=2026-09-23 |website=Kathmandu University |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Sharma was born in Khurkot village, [[Sindhuli District]] on 22 July 1940, to Bishnu Prasad Upadhyaya and Savitri Devi Dhungel. Bishnu Prasad Upadhyaya was a lawyer who, although born a Dhungel, chose to write Upadhyaya as his surname. Savitri Devi Dhungel was the sister of two brothers, the famous writer Kul Chandra Koirala and songwriter Divya Dev Koirala.{{citation needed|date=March 2025}}

He initially received education at home before setting out to study in [[Sonbarsa, Ballia|Sonbarsa, India]], in 1953, where he studied for nine months. In 2013 B.S. he passed his [[School Leaving Certificate (Nepal)|School Leaving Certificate]] examinations from Saraswati High School, Janakpur. After completing his I.Sc. and B.Sc. both from Public Science Campus (currently [[Amrit Science College]]) in the span of five years, Sharma went to study in [[Karnatak University]], India under the Colombo Plan Scholarship. Sharma then received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in Chemistry<ref>{{cite web | url=https://doi.org/10.18744/lsbu.94930 | doi=10.18744/lsbu.94930 | date=1977 | last1=Sharma | first1=Suresh Raj | title=Pharmacologically Active Principles in Extracts of Plants Suitable for Nepalese Horticulture }}</ref> from the Polytechnic of the South Bank, London, in 1977 (now London South Bank University).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Suresh Raj Sharma: Leadership Legacy |url=https://www.scribd.com/doc/144338030/Living-Legend-Dr-Suresh-Raj-Sharma |access-date=2026-09-23 |website=www.scribd.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=रहेनन् केयूका संस्थापक सुरेशराज शर्मा |url=https://ekantipur.com/news/2026/09/23/179018323302924233.html |access-date=2026-09-23 |website=Ekantipur |language=ne}}</ref>

== Career ==
Even before heading out to London for his Ph.D., Sharma had gained experience in academic and administrative areas. Sharma worked for twelve years as a professor in [[Tribhuvan University]] during which he also taught in Tri-Chandra College, Anandakuti College, Padma Kanya College and Nepal National College (currently Shankar Dev Campus). From 1989 to 1992, he worked as first executive director of the [[Council for Technical Education and Vocational Training]], which was conceptualized by himself.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A visionary educationalist |url=https://kathmandupost.com/miscellaneous/2018/02/19/a-visionary-educationalist |access-date=2026-09-23 |website=kathmandupost.com |language=English}}</ref> In the year 1991, he along with Sitaram Adhikary, Bhadra Man Tuladhar, and others successfully managed to charter Kathmandu University from Parliament. A month later, he was appointed the first-ever vice chancellor of the University.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-08 |title=Sharma appointed KU VC |url=https://myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com/news/sharma-appointed-ku-vc |access-date=2026-09-23 |website=myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com |language=English}}</ref>

In 2014 he was awarded an [[Honorary degree|honorary doctorate]] by the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ntnu.edu/phd/honorary-doctors|title=Honorary Doctors|website=www.ntnu.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-08-30}}</ref>

== Death ==
Sharma died on 23 September 2026, at the age of 86, while undergoing treatment at HAMS hospital in Kathmandu.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kathmandu University founding vice-chancellor Suresh Raj Sharma dies |url=https://kathmandupost.com/national/2026/09/23/kathmandu-university-founding-vice-chancellor-suresh-raj-sharma-dies |access-date=2026-09-23 |website=Kathmandu Post|language=en}}</ref> He was given a state funeral and was cremated the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Educationist Suresh Raj Sharma cremated with state honours |url=https://kathmandupost.com/national/2026/09/24/educationist-suresh-raj-sharma-cremated-with-state-honours |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=Kathmandu Post|language=en}}</ref>
